definition: Governance framework (Klakegg et al., 2008: S30) treated as public policy; neo-institutionalism (Scott's three pillars).
stakeholders: Treasury Board, deputy heads, project leaders, SDO, sponsor, Cabinet; actors added/removed each iteration.
decision_making: Yes - process tracing across five iterations.
temporality_detail: Core & RQ-critical. Five governance-framework iterations 1978-present mapped to changes of government (Liberal->Conservative->Liberal->Conservative->Liberal, Table 1); 'following the changes in the government parties, there have been... critical junctures... changes in vision and values' (p. 84).
misalignment_detail: Strongest demonstration that governance frameworks evolve with electoral/political alternation over decades - but framed as institutional layering/path dependency, not misalignment with a single project's timeline.
gaps: Framework-level (not single-project) trajectory; scale down to one megaproject crossing cycles.
key_quotes: 'following the changes in the government parties, there have been... critical junctures... changes in vision and values explicitly endorsed' (p. 84).
coding_notes: Same lead author as item 16 (Brunet 2021), distinct paper; shares Klakegg definition. Closest existing work to the RQ at framework scale.
